cards.explanation: The answer is those descending to the Pit, friends. David says, "For if You remain silent, I will be like those descending to the Pit." (Psalm 28:1) So when he calls the LORD his Rock and begs Him not to be deaf, I think he's feeling how much he needs an answer. David is the psalm's writer, and he doesn't hide how big this feels.

The answer is help, friends. David says he calls "…when I lift up my hands toward Your holy sanctuary." and the cry is for help. (Psalm 28:2) He asks the LORD to hear his cry for mercy, and he's not shy about it. Hands up, voice out, nothing held back.

The sneaky move is speaking peace with malice in the heart, friends. David says they "…speak peace to their neighbors while malice is in their hearts." (Psalm 28:3) Nice words on the outside, trouble on the inside. And David doesn't want to be dragged away with them.

The answer is False, friends. David asks the LORD, "Repay them according to their deeds and for their works of evil." (Psalm 28:4) He says it again: "Repay them for what their hands have done; bring back on them what they deserve." No letting off here. David is asking for repayment, and he asks twice.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "Since they show no regard for the works of the LORD or what His hands have done, He will tear them down and never rebuild them." (Psalm 28:5) The reason is right there in the verse. They ignore what the LORD has done.

The answer is mercy, friends. David says, "Blessed be the LORD, for He has heard my cry for mercy." (Psalm 28:6) That's the same kind of cry he made back in verse 2. He asked to be heard, and now he's blessing the LORD because he was.

The answer is that his heart trusts in Him, friends. David says, "my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped." (Psalm 28:7) The LORD is his strength and his shield, and his heart puts its trust in Him. That's the right place for it.

The answer is True, friends. David says, "Therefore my heart rejoices, and I give thanks to Him with my song." (Psalm 28:7) His heart is glad, and the gladness comes out in a song. I think I'd sing too, just not well.

The answer is people, friends. David says, "The LORD is the strength of His people…" (Psalm 28:8) The LORD was David's strength in verse 7, and now David says He's strength for all of His people. That's a big circle to draw around everybody.

The answer is shepherd them and carry them forever, friends! David prays, "Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever." (Psalm 28:9) And he says FOREVER. Friends, that's not a little favor. That's like asking someone to carry your groceries and then adding, "and the couch, and the whole move."
